subject: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@brightscale.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling

Alex — thanks again for the quick call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single playbook for the evaluation team at BrightScale.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: confirm Redwood delivers feature parity for your three must-haves (tool/function calling, structured JSON outputs, server-side streaming) while staying within your latency/cost targets.
- Secondary: procurement needs a simple contract/terms outline and a list of security artifacts.

Proposed pragmatic probe (small, measurable tests)
1) Tool/function calling: run the same 6-step workflow you demoed (lookup user, fetch pricing, call external billing API, enrich response). Measure success rate, average end-to-end latency, and failure handling for: Redwood hosted API, Redwood Private (container), and CloudVendor-managed endpoint (your hyperscaler proof-of-concept).
2) Structured outputs: give us 20 representative prompts and gold JSON schemas; we'll run 1k generations across models and report schema conformance + edit distance on key fields.
3) Streaming: stream a 500-token response to see jitter, reconnect behavior, and partial-output usability.

Deliverables and timeline
- Redwood will provide: a parity matrix template (attached), a short test harness (instructions + curl/SDK examples), and test accounts/keys.
- BrightScale will provide: canonical prompt set, example tool definitions, and an official contact for procurement.
- Timeline: target test window 7/6–7/10, with a 30m sync on 7/13 to review results.

Attachments: parity-probe-plan.md (high-level runbook), parity-matrix.xlsx (matrix + metric columns).

Next step for today: can you confirm the test window works and that procurement (copied) should receive the contract summary? If you'd like, Monica can own the set-up and initial keys.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: parity-probe-plan.md (text/markdown)]
[Attachment: parity-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightscale.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightscale.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 12:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling

Thanks, Sean — this is exactly the format we like. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Test window: 7/6–7/10 looks good but we need the harness up by 7/2 so our infra team can sanity-check. Can Redwood provision both a hosted test key and a private trial container image for our on-prem evaluator?
2) Tool chain detail: our billing API requires a signed JWT to call the sandbox endpoint. Will your tool-calling harness support a client-signed JWT (we can provide a test key)?
3) Procurement: please include a short MSA/terms summary (1 page) and a SOC2 attestation doc. Procurement is looped in; they’ll expect a redline window of ~5 business days after we send a PO.

Alex
Alex Rivera | Head of ML Platforms, BrightScale
alex@brightscale.com

P.S. CC'd Sam Tang from CloudVendor to observe the streaming test (Sam, feel free to forward any latency telemetry templates you prefer).

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@brightscale.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightscale.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling

Alex — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers and actions: 

1) Provisioning: yes — we will:
   - Spin up a short-lived hosted test key (scope: parity-tests) by 7/2.
   - Provide a Redwood Private evaluation container and a checklist to run it in a sandbox (image + k8s manifest).
2) JWT/tool-calling: our SDK supports custom auth handlers; we’ll add a small example showing how to sign requests with a client JWT and wire it into the tool-calling adapter.
3) Docs for procurement: attaching the one-page MSA summary and SOC2 pointer. Expect a formal doc package by EOD 7/2.

I've attached the parity matrix populated with the columns we discussed (feature, pass/fail, latency_ms p50/p95, cost token-estimate, notes). Please review and add any BrightScale columns we should include (e.g., compliance checks).

Proposed schedule: 7/2 — infra sanity + keys; 7/6–7/10 — test window; 7/13 — results sync.

I'll own provisioning and will post the test credentials in the secure channel (we'll avoid email for secrets).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: parity-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: MSA-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@brightscale.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightscale.com>, Sam Tang <sam.tang@cloudvendor.io>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling

Quick note — thanks for the confirmations. Two tactical items from the Redwood side before 7/2: 

- I'll send a short demo pack (curl + Node + Python snippets) that exercises tool calling with a JWT. Expect that in your inbox by 7/2 11:00 PST.
- Lauren will own the streaming test harness (capturing partial-chunk timing and reconnect). Lauren — can you drop the telemetry schema and a sample script in the shared Drive folder by EOD tomorrow?

Alex — is there a particular latency SLO we should aim for in the p95 path for your user flows? If you can give us a target, we'll prioritize model and batching settings that hit it during the probe.

Thanks — looking forward to the results.

—Sean
[Attachment: demo-snippets.tar.gz (application/gzip) — will be posted to Drive]

From: Alex Rivera <alex@brightscale.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightscale.com>, Sam Tang <sam.tang@cloudvendor.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 23:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: Parity probe & pragmatic next tests for tool/function calling

Thanks — that all sounds good. Target p95 latency for our user-critical flow is <= 350ms (end-to-end tool invocation including the external billing sandbox). If Redwood can show consistent p95 <= 350ms in the hosted test and explain any delta we see on the Private container, we'll be in a good spot.

Procurement: when you get a moment, please confirm the billing contact who will issue the PO and whether BrightScale legal needs an additional NDA.

Sam — if you can share the telemetry template you use for streaming jitter, that will help us compare measurements between CloudVendor and Redwood.

I'll review the parity matrix and drop any additional prompts by 7/2 morning.

—Alex
